goal.statement: Bake a sourdough loaf with an open crumb, and diagnose it when it comes out dense.
goal.audience: someone who has baked with yeast but never with a starter

capstone.prompt: Bake a loaf. If the crumb comes out tight, say which stage caused it and what you would change next time.
rubric: names the stage, not just the symptom

kcs.label: Identify the correct baking schedule based on room temperature
misconceptions: Room temperature doesn't affect fermentation rate
All sourdough is baked on a strict timeline
Timing is flexible regardless of temperature

check.stem: How does room temperature affect your sourdough baking schedule?
options: Room temperature is irrelevant to baking schedule
All sourdough bakes on the same timeline
Higher temperatures speed up fermentation, requiring a shorter schedule
Temperature doesn't matter; adjust based on recipe
distractorSource: Room temperature doesn't affect fermentation rate
All sourdough is baked on a strict timeline
Timing is flexible regardless of temperature

kcs.label: Choose and maintain a starter with appropriate strength
misconceptions: All starters have the same feeding routine
A starter's feeding schedule doesn't affect bread structure
Starters don't need to be active to bake

check.stem: What role does maintaining an active starter play in sourdough baking?
options: All feeding routines are the same
Starter activity doesn't affect the outcome
Inactive starters can still bake perfectly
An active starter helps ensure proper rise and crumb structure
distractorSource: All starters have the same feeding routine
A starter's feeding schedule doesn't affect bread structure
Starters don't need to be active to bake

kcs.label: Mix and knead dough to develop gluten structure
misconceptions: The more kneading, the better the bread
Gluten doesn't need development in sourdough

check.stem: Why is it important to develop gluten in sourdough dough?
options: Proper gluten development is crucial for structure and crumb
Gluten development doesn't matter
Kneading is unnecessary
More kneading always improves bread
distractorSource: Gluten doesn't need development in sourdough
The more kneading, the better the bread

kcs.label: Shape dough correctly for final proof
misconceptions: Over-handling dough doesn't impact final loaf

check.stem: What is the purpose of correctly shaping sourdough?
options: It's only for looks
Proper shaping helps maintain structure and even baking
Handling doesn't affect outcome
One shaping method fits all
distractorSource: Over-handling dough doesn't impact final loaf

kcs.label: Bake the loaf at the correct temperature and time
misconceptions: All breads bake at the same temperature
Baking time won't affect loaf texture
Oven temperature doesn't need strict control

check.stem: Why is it important to bake sourdough at specific temperatures and times?
options: Baking temperature is universally the same
Time doesn't impact loaf texture
Correct baking ensures proper texture and crust development
Strict temperature control is unnecessary
distractorSource: All breads bake at the same temperature
Baking time won't affect loaf texture
Oven temperature doesn't need strict control

kcs.label: Analyze crumb texture and diagnose potential issues
misconceptions: A tight crumb is unavoidable in sourdough
Crumb issues are always due to starter
Dough hydration doesn't affect crumb openness

check.stem: What are possible reasons for a tight crumb in a sourdough loaf?
options: Tight crumb is inevitable
It's always due to the starter
Hydration doesn't matter
Under-proofing, insufficient kneading, or low hydration can cause tight crumb
distractorSource: A tight crumb is unavoidable in sourdough
Crumb issues are always due to starter
Dough hydration doesn't affect crumb openness
